newsitem.title: USA: U.S. LPG mostly down as buyers duck high prices.
newsitem.headline: U.S. LPG mostly down as buyers duck high prices.

text.p: U.S. buyers were ducking high prices prices in the liquefied petroleum gas (LPG) market, making for for wafer-thin trading early Monday, traders said.
"It's a non-event," one Belvieu trader said. "There's a continued lack of direction in the MERC (New York Mercantile Exchange) and in buyers' minds prices are probably still too high."

Belvieu propane was pegged about a quarter-cent lower than Friday at 36.50/36.75 cents a gallon, traders said. Few deals were heard done, but a small parcel for September was done at 37.00 cents, and October was heard done a quarter-cent higher.
Current month Belvieu ethane purity was heard done at 22 cents.
With the exception of propane, trading in the Conway, Kansas market was also lean. Propane was heard done at 36.50 and 36.63 cents, no higher than material was pegged by the end of last week.

One Conway trader said prices for the gasoline blendstocks butane and natural gasoline were too high to find any buying interest. Butane was pegged about a half-cent higher than Friday at 41.50/41.75 cents. Natural gasoline was slightly lower than Friday, pegged at 46.50/47.00 cents.
